text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The foreign ministers of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia discussed their NATO strategies on the Estonian island of Saaremaa at the week-end and called on the alliance to pledge that its first round of enlargement will not be its last.

- A new national conservative party - the National Party of Reforms - was created on Saturday by several local groups of the LNNK opposed to the party's merger with the radical nationalist party Fatherland & Freedom.
- The 6th congress of the Association of Latvia's local governments on Saturday passed several resolutions voicing concern over planned administrative reforms.
- A private armed with a Kalashnikov machine gun went AWOL from the Adazhi training center on the night of May 30. By Sunday afternoon he was still at large.

- American Latvian and Baltic community leader, Janis Kukainis, was assured in a letter by U.S. President Bill Clinton that no country will be allowed to veto the expansion of NATO and no nation will be banned from joining the alliance.
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele says his visit to Moscow now depends on the Russian side.
- The joint stock company Baltijas Holdings, owned by two former ministers and close business partners, Eriks Kazha and Vassily Melnik, has bought a 60-percent stake in Ogre knitwear plant.
- The port of Liepaja has started the reconstruction of its southern pier, due to be finished by September 30.
